[0] everyday_reading (E): In arithmetic, + always means 'add', and 'plus' combines quantities, so novices expect "1" + 2 to be 3. In Java, + with a String operand joins text end to end, and a chain of + is processed left to right, one operator at a time.
[1] misconception (M) -> StringPlusStringifiesExpression: wrong rule: + with a String turns the whole other side into a string first. Right rule: The expression (a + b) is evaluated first, and its value is then turned into text and joined to s.
[2] misconception (M) -> StringPlusLeftToRight: wrong rule: 2 + 3 + "bc" and "bc" + 2 + 3 give the same text. Right rule: + is evaluated left to right: 2 + 3 + "bc" is "5bc" but "bc" + 2 + 3 is "bc23".
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> StringPlusStringifiesExpression: Points to LT (left to right, and each + adds or concatenates according to its operands at that moment). Applied unevenly, a student keeps adding numbers after a String has appeared, or concatenates before any String appears (1 + 2 + "x" as "12x"). (here mixing in: "+ with a String turns the whole other side into a string first")
[4] misconception (M) -> ArithmeticPlusPrecedes: wrong rule: arithmetic + binds tighter than string-concatenation +. Right rule: Both uses of + have the same precedence and are evaluated left to right, so "s" + a + b joins a and then b as text; only "s" + (a + b) adds them first.

[0] names_the_element (N): String concatenation: the + operator with a String operand, which joins two values end to end into a new String.
[1] states_the_rule (S): If either operand of + is a String, the other is converted to a String, and the result is a new String made of the first operand's characters followed by the second's.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): A chain of + is evaluated left to right, after any parenthesized parts. At each + the current operand types decide: two numbers are added, otherwise the values are concatenated.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The result is a String: 2 + "bc" is "2bc", 2 + 3 + "bc" is "5bc", "bc" + 2 + 3 is "bc23", and "bc" + (2+3) is "bc5".
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Concatenation creates a new String and changes no operand. A variable changes only if the result is assigned, as in ruler = ruler + i + ruler;.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Concatenation always yields a String, even when one operand is a number, so its result cannot be used in arithmetic without parsing.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): The non-String operand is converted to its printed form (int 99 to "99", double 1.0 to "1.0", char 'a' to "a") before joining.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): + adds when both operands are numbers and concatenates when either operand is a String, converting the other operand to a String. It is left-associative, so 1 + 2 + "3" is "33" but "1" + 2 + 3 is "123".
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Concatenation builds output lines and labels from computed values (a + " + " + b + " = " + c). Repeated s = s + piece makes s a gatherer of text.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> StringPlusStringifiesExpression: Parenthesizing numeric parts changes the result ("sum " + (a + b) adds before joining). Moving numbers before or after the first String changes whether they are added. Concatenating into a printf format string removes the separate argument printf needs.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use + concatenation for simple output and labels, putting parentheses around any arithmetic inside. Use printf when numbers need formatting, and parse Strings before using them as numbers.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Once a String appears in a + chain, every later + concatenates. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: "Sum: " + a + b with numbers a and b prints both digit strings side by side (e.g. Sum: 23).
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: char + char is numeric addition, not concatenation. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Joining two chars with + when no String is involved ('b' + 'c' prints 197).
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: printf needs its values as separate arguments matching the format specifiers. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Concatenating the value into the format (printf("inches = %d" + inch)): MissingFormatArgumentException.

+ adds when both operands are numbers and concatenates when either operand is a String, converting the other operand to a String. It is left-associative, so 1 + 2 + "3" is "33" but "1" + 2 + 3 is "123".
When one operand of + is a String, Java converts the other operand to a String before concatenating.
+ builds a new String whenever at least one of its operands is a String.
